messages.text: miner over heating

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist, happy to help with the heat.

To point you the right way, which model is it (NerdQaxe++, NerdOctaxe, Bitaxe, something else), and what temperature is the web UI showing?

NerdQX (8TH/s)

Miner overheated guru mediation with some number
Searched the web · NerdQaxe Guru Meditation Error overheat ESP32 reboot
Read github.com/shufps/qaxe/issues

Thanks, that helps. On the NerdQX the "Guru Meditation" screen is the firmware stopping the ASIC on purpose and showing an error number, and the number tells us which protection tripped. I do not want to guess which one you have.

Two things, then I will give you the exact next step:

1. The exact text and number on the screen (a photo of the display is perfect). On these boards I have seen "VREG Overheated Guru Meditation #····" (voltage regulator trip) and "PSU Error Guru Meditation #····", and they mean different things. 
The #···· one is logged as a VR temperature reading at the moment ASIC voltage is enabled, after which voltage drops to 0V
, while 
#···· has shown up as a PSU error that reboots away and came back with a firmware rollback
.
2. The firmware version shown in the web UI (bottom of the page, something like v1.0.3x).

Also useful while you grab those: is it a stock power supply, and is the unit stock clocked or overclocked?
GB5A5A00
Searched the web · NerdQaxe "Guru Meditation" "5A5A" error code display

I could not find "GB5A5A00" as a NerdQX error code anywhere in the firmware docs or issue tracker, so I will not guess at it. The codes I can verify on these boards look like #···· (VREG overheated) or #···· (PSU error), so what you read may be a partial or misread line.

Could you send a photo of the display showing the full line, plus the firmware version from the web UI? With the exact string I can tell you which protection tripped and what to do about it.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Thanks, that photo settles it. Let me check the firmware source for how that number is built before I tell you what it means.
Searched the web · ESP-Miner-NerdQAxePlus "MINER OVERHEATED" overheat_mode sour
Searched the web · NerdQAxe++ "Guru Meditation #4B" overheat code meaning tempe
Read github.com/shufps/ESP-Miner-NerdQAxePlus/issues/707

Opened it. The screen reads: MINER OVERHEATED, Guru Meditation #4B5A5A00, BM1370 chips, 63 C, 132.750 W, 16.5 W/TH, 8049.0 GH/s. So the board is at spec power and efficiency, and the temperature showing now (63 C) is fine, which means the firmware latched an overheat trip earlier and stopped hashing rather than the unit being hot right now.

On the number itself: I will not claim a meaning I cannot source. The published examples I can verify are #···· (VREG overheated) and #···· (PSU error), and 
in the VREG case the firmware logged a single very high regulator reading (127.88 C) at the instant ASIC voltage was enabled, then cut voltage to 0 V even though the regulator was not actually hot
. Yours is a different byte pattern, so I am asking JD to confirm the exact decode rather than guess.

One check first, this is the one that decides it: with the unit powered, are both fans actually spinning, and what fan speed / RPM does the web UI show? If you can, tell me the firmware version on the same page too.

Fan speed 100%
Fan RPM (postal code ····) temp 49.2
asic temp 54.2, 51.7, 63.1, 52.3
asic Frequency 1000MHZ

Good data, that narrows it a lot.

Two things stand out:

1. 1000 MHz is well above the stock clock for an 8 TH NerdQX, so this unit is running an overclock preset. The overheat trip is latched from an earlier spike, not from what the board shows now.
2. Your chip temperatures are uneven: 54.2 / 51.7 / 63.1 / 52.3. A single chip about 10 C hotter than its neighbours usually means that chip has weaker heatsink contact or sits in a dead spot of the airflow. Under an overclock that hot chip is the one that hits the trip threshold first.

Fan at 100 percent and only 1697 RPM is also on the low side, which fits a restricted or partly blocked airflow path.

One step now: in the web UI set the frequency and core voltage back to the stock preset (the default for your board, not the overclock), save, and reboot the unit. Let it run 20 to 30 minutes and tell me the four ASIC temps and the VR temp again, plus the firmware version from that same page.

If it stays up at stock, we are chasing cooling on that one chip. If it trips again at stock, that is a hardware issue and I take it further.
I didnt change anything, i just plugged it in so i guess its all default?

Understood, and thanks for saying so. Then scratch my overclock assumption: on the 8 TH NerdQX 1000 MHz is likely the factory default, so the unit is running as shipped. That makes the uneven chip temperature the real lead: 63.1 C on one chip against about 52 C on the other three is a bigger spread than a healthy board should show, and that chip is what trips the overheat guard.

Two quick things and I will tell you what it is:

1. The firmware version from the web UI (I still need this one).
2. Where it sits: room temperature, and is it in open air or in a cabinet, shelf or enclosure with anything near the fan intake or exhaust?

Then reboot it, let it hash, and watch that third chip: tell me the temperature it reaches just before it trips again.
Ok how do I set this up for solo mining? What is the wallet address any guide?
Searched the web · public-pool.io stratum port 21496 solo.ckpool.org 3333 bitax

Happy to set that up. Short version: solo mining means pointing the miner at a solo pool and using your own Bitcoin address as the username, so if your unit finds a block the reward goes to you.

The wallet address has to be yours, we never give one out and nobody from HeliumDeploy will ever send you an address to mine to. Get a Bitcoin wallet you control (Sparrow, Blue Wallet, Electrum, or a hardware wallet), copy its receive address (starts with bc1 or 1 or 3), and use that.

In the miner web UI, Settings, pool configuration:

1. Stratum host: solo.ckpool.org, port 3333, password x. 
Our own guide uses solo.ckpool.org on port 3333 with the password x, and says to set the fallback pool the same way.

2. Alternative with a nicer dashboard and low difficulty shares: 
stratum+tcp://public-pool.io:21496, 0 percent fee
.
3. Stratum user: your address, optionally with a worker name after a dot, like bc1yourAddress.nerdqx1.
4. Save and reboot, then check the pool site for your address to confirm shares arriving.

Full written guide: https://heliumdeploy.com/blogs/mining-news/bitaxe-solo-mining-setup-guide

One caution: double check the address you paste, character for character. A mistyped address means the pool keeps anything found.

And we still have the overheat trip open. When you get a moment, the firmware version and whether it trips again after a reboot, plus the temperature that hot chip reaches before it stops.
ew

Not sure which part got the "ew", so tell me and I will fix it.

If it is the wallet step: it is a one time thing, and the easiest route is Blue Wallet on a phone, tap receive, copy the address, paste it as the stratum user. Nothing else to configure.

If it is the overheat trip still hanging over you: that is the one I want to close out. When you are back at the miner, send me the firmware version and whether it trips again after a reboot.
hello

Hello, still here.

Where we are: your NerdQX latched a MINER OVERHEATED trip (Guru Meditation #4B5A5A00) while one chip ran about 10 C hotter than the other three, and we set up solo mining pointing at your own wallet address.

Two things left on the heat side, whenever you are at the unit:

1. The firmware version from the web UI.
2. Reboot it, let it hash, and tell me if it trips again and what that hot chip reaches first.

If you would rather not wait on me, the Discord is quick for this: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead).
I want to setup Bitcoin cash solo mining - but i am consfued about wallet.modelname as what is my model name? NerdQX (BM1370) so what would that translate into?
Searched the web · Bitcoin Cash solo mining pool stratum bitaxe NerdQaxe BCH ad

Good question, and the answer is simpler than it looks: the part after the dot is not a model code. It is a worker name you invent yourself, purely a label so you can tell your machines apart on the pool dashboard. The pool does not care what it says.

So for yours, anything works: nerdqx, nerdqx8t, bm1370, garage1. Only the address before the dot matters for payment.

One rule: keep it to letters, numbers, dash or underscore. 
On some pools the worker name must contain only letters, numbers, - or _, and a + will be rejected
.

For BCH solo specifically, your NerdQX is SHA-256 so it mines BCH fine, you just need a BCH address and a BCH endpoint:

1. 
NexusPool BCH: stratum+tcp://bch.nexuspool.io:3351, username your BCH address (CashAddr or legacy) plus worker, password x
.
2. 
SoloFury also runs BCH endpoints, port 7333 standard
, 
at a 1 percent fee
.

So your stratum user would look like: qr8yourBchAddress.nerdqx

One caution worth knowing: 
some stock pool software mishandles a bare CashAddr without the bitcoincash: prefix, which can silently misdirect rewards
. If the pool accepts the prefixed form, use it, and after it connects check the pool page shows your address.
